title: Supervised and unsupervised data mining approaches in loan default prediction
authors: Alejandrino, J.C.; Bolacoy, J.P.; Murcia, J.V.B.
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
tldr: Comparing supervised and unsupervised classifiers on a Philippine cooperative loan dataset, k-NN 3 and logistic regression achieved the highest classification accuracies of 78.38% and 77.31%.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions in the Philippines lack data-driven recommender systems to predict loan defaults due to regulatory constraints, despite high default incidences reducing collection efficiency.
approach: Dataset of 1,000 loan records from a Philippine cooperative with 29 attributes, split into 900 training and 100 test instances.
Missing values imputed using mean for numeric and mode for nominal attributes; two constant-value attributes and ID removed.
Numeric attributes normalized to [0,1] range using Weka's unsupervised instance filter to improve classifier reliability.
Three feature selection methods—correlation, information gain, and learner-based—were applied to identify the most relevant attributes.
SMOTE oversampling increased the minority class from 250 to 650 instances to address class imbalance, yielding 1,300 training instances.
Four classifiers evaluated: J48 decision tree, k-NN, naive Bayes, and logistic regression, with parameter tuning on k and confidence factor.
Thirteen-fold cross-validation on balanced training data with performance assessed using F-measure, accuracy, and kappa statistic.
Best classifiers selected based on highest accuracy, F-measure, and kappa, then applied to the 100-instance unlabeled test set.
findings: num: k-NN 3 achieved 78.38% classification accuracy with F-measure of 0.780 and kappa of 0.5677.
num: Logistic regression achieved 77.31% accuracy with F-measure of 0.773 and kappa of 0.5462.
num: J48 with 0.50 confidence factor was best among decision tree variants at 76.85% accuracy.
num: Naive Bayes achieved 76.65% accuracy with F-measure of 0.765 and kappa of 0.5308.
k-NN 3 predicted 48 non-defaulters and 52 defaulters on the 100-instance test set.
Logistic predicted 44 non-defaulters and 56 defaulters on the test set.
Increasing k in k-NN beyond 3 consistently decreased F-measure, accuracy, and kappa statistics.
num: SMOTE increased minority class instances by 160%, from 250 to 650, enabling balanced 13-fold cross-validation.
key_figures_tables: Table 2: Classification accuracy of 11 classifier variants on training dataset → k-NN 3 and logistic achieved highest accuracy.
Figure 2: Confusion matrices for all classifier variants → Shows distribution of correct and incorrect class predictions.
Table 3: Summary of F-measure, accuracy, and kappa across classifiers → k-NN 3 leads all three metrics.
Figure 3: Kappa statistic and MAE for J48 variants → J48 with 0.50 confidence factor has highest kappa.
Figure 4: F-measure and MAE for IBk variants → k-NN 3 has highest F-measure and lowest MAE.
Figure 1: Descriptive statistics of attribute A10 before and after normalization → Normalization rescaled values to [0,1] range.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper contributes a comparative evaluation of four supervised data mining classifiers for loan default prediction using real-world data from a Philippine cooperative.
directly_justifies: k-NN 3 achieved 78.38% classification accuracy, the highest among all tested classifiers.
SMOTE increased minority class by 160% to address class imbalance in training.
Two attributes eliminated as they showed no variation relevant to class prediction.
k-NN 3 predicted 48 non-defaulters and 52 defaulters on the unlabeled test set.
J48 with 0.50 confidence factor performed best among decision tree variants.
